text.en: Domain-aware, double-exponential and sparse-grid quadrature Compare fixed integrals with domain-aware methods, separating estimated errors, actual errors, budget exits and underresolution controls. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-quadrature-controls-2026-11-25 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. QUADPACK dispatch and finite Simpson companions Fifteen specialized quadratures and fifteen Simpson companions use fixed inputs. The formulas and inputs specify mathematical integration domains and dimensions. Parameter and error axes are not physical spatial coordinates. Passing reproduction checks does not mean that every accuracy goal was met. Original row outcomes: 25 met, 2 unmet and 3 not computable. False/NA outcomes and raw failures are retained. Adopted numerical method Explicit domain/weight dispatch retains active full_output prefixes. The existing Simpson function is unchanged. I=∫Ωf(x) dx References and measured quantities Independent analytic interval references and actual callback counts are checked. The finite Gaussian target is an interval, not an invented erf value. Verification limits and failures Singular-node failures and unmet Simpson goals remain visible; error estimates are not general guarantees.
